Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our call so we have alignment on the HIPAA/BAA questions you raised.

Recap
- Primary ask: confirm whether MedWise can process PHI on Redwood and which deployment modes are eligible (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).
- You asked for SOC 2 evidence and a draft BAA to share with procurement/security.
- MedWise also had a short vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) you'll attach.

High-level answers (we will provide more detail + docs below):
- BAA: Redwood can sign a BAA for eligible customers, but eligibility depends on deployment mode and controls.
- PHI handling: Recommended/eligible modes for PHI are Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC or on-prem). Our standard multi-tenant Hosted API is not approved for PHI unless we put explicit contractual and architectural controls in place, we can discuss exceptions with Security/Legal, but plan for Dedicated/Private.
- Controls available: KMS/HSM key management options, audit logs, retention/export controls, and optional on-prem deployment for air-gapped environments.

Attachments I'm including with this note:
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_Summary_2026.pdf (SOC 2 Type II summary)
- Redwood_BAA_Template_v1.docx (BAA template we typically use)

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll share the SOC2 summary + BAA template (attached).
2) Please send your VSQ and any specific security controls you need (you mentioned sending that after the call).
3) Schedule a 30-45 minute security deep-dive with our infra/security engineers (we've found this helps clarify network/KMS/audit expectations quickly). Suggested times: Thu 3/3 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 3/4 9:00-10:00 PT, tell me what works for your team.

If helpful, Dev (cc'd) can jump in with details on Dedicated vs Private configuration and what we lock down for PHI workloads.

Thanks, talk soon.

Alex,

Quick answers and more detail from the infra side. Happy to cover any of this on the deep-dive.

1) Hosted (multi-tenant) and PHI:
- Our standard hosted public API is considered a multi-tenant endpoint and by default is not approved for PHI. We can consider exceptions, but those require Legal/Security review and custom contractual controls; plan for Dedicated or Private for a faster path to compliance.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) and PHI:
- Dedicated runs in tenant-isolated GPU pools assigned to a single customer. Model weights are the same, but inference instances, KV caches, and request routing are isolated to your capacity slice.
- Persistence: by default we do not persist request-level PHI beyond the configured retention window. We will provide retention settings (including zero-retention options) and the ability to export logs.
- Key management: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS/HSM is supported for encryption at rest/rotation.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem) and PHI:
- Private deployment (VPC-connected control plane + customer-managed compute or on-prem package) is the gold standard for PHI. You control networking, and access to logs and keys remains with your team.
- Support model: we offer an ops channel with limited remote access for upgrades/patches (can be scheduled and limited to a maintenance window); all access is logged. For fully air-gapped on-prem installs we operate via an agreed change/package process.

4) Other controls we typically configure for HIPAA customers:
- Audit logs with export to your SIEM
- Role-based access controls and MFA for all operator accounts
- Optional model quantization/lock-down for model artifact immutability

Next steps (recommendation):
- MedWise to return the completed VSQ (attached in your email).
- We'll prepare a DocuSign-ready BAA once Legal approves the template for your account (I'll coordinate internally).
- Scheduling: Dev and one of our security engineers + Marissa will join the deep-dive. Proposed times are the same as Marissa suggested; please let us know which slot works and include Sarah.

If you want, I can also put together a short matrix comparing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (controls, expected lead time, typical costs) and attach it to the procurement thread.

Thanks,
